howItWorks.title: From key file to submitted batch
howItWorks.description: IndexNow has four moving parts. Each step below maps to a tool on this site, so you can go from an empty domain to a verified submission without writing a script.

steps.title: Generate a key
steps.description: Create an 8–128 character key made of letters, digits and dashes. Anything random and long enough works — the key is an ownership proof, not a secret credential.

steps.title: Host the key file
steps.description: Upload a plain-text file containing only the key to https://your-host/your-key.txt. Search engines fetch this file to confirm you control the host.

steps.title: Prepare a single-host batch
steps.description: IndexNow accepts one host per request and up to 10,000 URLs. Remove duplicates and split mixed-host lists before you submit.

steps.title: Submit only what changed
steps.description: Notifying unchanged URLs wastes quota. Compare sitemaps to isolate new and updated pages, then submit that queue.

responseCodes.title: IndexNow response codes
responseCodes.description: What each status from the IndexNow endpoint means, and what to change before you retry.

items.label: OK
items.action: Nothing to do. Indexing is neither guaranteed nor immediate — the engine still decides what to crawl and keep.

items.label: Accepted
items.meaning: URL received, key validation still pending.
items.action: Verify the key file is reachable. If validation later fails, the submission is discarded without another response.

items.label: Bad request
items.action: Check the request body: host, key and urlList must all be present and well-formed.

items.label: Forbidden
items.meaning: The key could not be validated.
items.action: The key file is missing, unreachable, or its content does not match the submitted key. Run the key checker.

items.label: Unprocessable Entity
items.meaning: URLs do not belong to the host, or the key does not match the protocol schema.
items.action: Every URL must be on the host you declared. Split mixed-host lists into separate requests.

items.label: Too Many Requests
items.meaning: Too many requests, treated as potential spam.
items.action: Slow down and submit only changed URLs. Repeatedly re-submitting a full sitemap triggers this.

items.question: Does IndexNow guarantee my page gets indexed?
items.answer: No. IndexNow tells participating engines that a URL changed, which removes the discovery delay. Whether the page is indexed still depends on the engine’s own quality, canonical, robots, and crawl-budget checks.

items.question: Which search engines and AI search tools receive my submission?
items.answer: One request to api.indexnow.org or Bing is shared across all IndexNow participants — Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz, Naver, and Yep. Because Bing’s index powers Microsoft Copilot and informs ChatGPT Search, timely IndexNow pings also accelerate AI search discovery.

items.question: Does IndexNow help with ChatGPT Search and Microsoft Copilot visibility?
items.answer: Yes, indirectly through discovery speed. Bing’s index feeds Microsoft Copilot and supports ChatGPT Search web retrieval. Pair IndexNow with clean robots.txt access for Bingbot and OAI-SearchBot and avoid unintended noindex directives.

items.question: Why doesn’t IndexNow cover Google, and what should I use for Google?
items.answer: Google does not participate in IndexNow, and Google’s Indexing API is officially restricted to JobPosting and BroadcastEvent pages. For Google, keep an accurate XML sitemap with reliable lastmod dates in Google Search Console and use URL Inspection for critical single-page recrawls.

items.question: How many URLs can I send at once?
items.answer: The IndexNow protocol allows up to 10,000 same-host URLs per HTTP request. When you paste or import more than 10,000 same-host URLs in submitnow, the form automatically splits and submits them in sequential 10,000-URL batches.

items.question: Is my IndexNow key a secret?
items.answer: No. The key file is public by design — search engines fetch it over plain HTTP to verify you control the host. Treat it as an ownership token, not a credential.

items.question: Can I use one key for several domains?
items.answer: Yes, if you host the same key file on each domain. Every request still covers a single host, so submit each domain separately. You can save multiple site profiles locally on your device.

items.question: Where should the key file live?
items.answer: The root — https://your-host/your-key.txt — authorizes every URL on the host. A key file inside a subdirectory (such as /blog/key.txt) only authorizes URLs under that exact directory prefix.

items.question: Does submitnow store my key or my URLs?
items.answer: No. Requests are forwarded server-side without storing keys or URLs in any database. Optional multi-site profiles, sitemap baselines, and history exports stay strictly inside your browser’s localStorage.

items.question: How often should I submit?
items.answer: Only when content actually changes (new, updated, or deleted pages). Use Sitemap Diff or the lastmod filter to send delta-only batches and avoid triggering HTTP 429 rate limits.

whenToUse.title: When to use submitnow IndexNow Key Generator
whenToUse.intro: An IndexNow key is an ownership proof: a random string you publish on your own host so search engines can confirm a submission comes from someone who controls that host. You need a new key in a few situations.

items.title: Setting up a new host
items.description: Every hostname you submit URLs for needs a key file it can serve. A staging domain and a production domain are two different hosts.

items.title: Rotating after a mistake
items.description: The key is public, but a key file that also exists on a domain you do not control is worthless. Generate a new one and remove the old file.

items.title: Separating environments
items.description: Distinct keys per environment make it obvious which system submitted a batch when you audit logs later.

items.title: Replacing a weak key
items.description: Short or guessable keys either fail the protocol's 8–128 character rule or make the file trivial to reproduce. A generated key avoids both.

howTo.title: How to generate and install an IndexNow key with submitnow
howTo.intro: The key never leaves your browser: it is produced with the Web Crypto API and the download is assembled locally.

steps.title: Generate the key
steps.description: You get a 48-character hexadecimal string — well inside the protocol's 8–128 character limit, and made only of characters IndexNow accepts.

steps.title: Download the text file
steps.description: The file is named <key>.txt and contains the key and nothing else. Extra content is the single most common cause of a 403.

steps.title: Upload it to your host root
steps.description: Serve it at https://your-host/your-key.txt as text/plain. Confirm it is not behind auth, a redirect, or a bot-protection challenge.

steps.title: Verify, then submit
steps.description: Run the key checker against the live URL before your first batch. Once it passes, paste the same key into the submission form.

items.title: The file contains more than the key
items.description: A trailing newline is fine; a template wrapper, JSON, or an HTML page is not. The file body must equal the key.

items.title: The host serves a soft 404
items.description: Many frameworks answer unknown paths with a 200 and the app shell. Search engines then read HTML instead of the key and reject the batch.

items.title: The key is treated as a secret
items.description: Putting the file behind auth or blocking it in robots rules defeats its purpose — verification is an unauthenticated HTTP fetch.

items.title: One key reused without the file
items.description: Each host must serve its own copy. A key that validates on example.com does not authorise blog.example.com.

items.question: How long should an IndexNow key be?
items.answer: Between 8 and 128 characters, using letters, digits and dashes. This tool produces 48 hexadecimal characters — long enough to be unguessable, short enough to stay readable in logs.

items.question: Can I write the key myself?
items.answer: Yes. Any string within the character and length rules works. A generated key simply avoids accidentally picking something short or predictable.

items.question: Does the file name have to match the key?
items.answer: Only if you rely on the default location. If you host the file elsewhere, pass that URL as keyLocation when you submit — it must still be on the same host.

items.question: Is the key sent to submitnow when I generate it?
items.answer: No. Generation and download happen entirely in your browser; there is no network request at all.

items.question: How often should I rotate the key?
items.answer: There is no expiry. Rotate only when you need to invalidate an old file, and remember to delete the previous key file afterwards.

keyChecker.metaDescription: Verify an IndexNow key file from the public internet. Detects 404s, soft 404s, off-host redirects, empty files and key mismatches before you submit a batch.
keyChecker.title: Check that your IndexNow key file is valid
keyChecker.description: Fetch your key file the way a search engine does and see exactly why verification would fail: wrong status, off-host redirect, HTML instead of text, or a key that does not match.
keyChecker.privacyNote: This check runs on submitnow’s stateless server because public key files must be fetched from outside your network, exactly as a search engine would. Only that URL is requested, and nothing is stored.
keyChecker.formHelp: Enter the host you submit URLs for and the key you plan to use. The default file location is derived automatically.

keyChecker.keyLocationHelp: Only needed when the file is not at https://host/key.txt. It must still be on the same host.
keyChecker.resultInvalid: This key file would fail verification.
checklist: Answers 200 over HTTPS on the same host as your URLs.
Contains the key as plain text, with no markup and nothing else.
Is reachable without cookies, authentication or a bot challenge.
Does not redirect to a different hostname.
Stays online — engines re-check it on later submissions.
keyChecker.serverFetchNote: Browsers cannot read a cross-origin plain-text response, so this is the one tool here that must run server-side.

not_found.title: File not found (404).
not_found.fix: Upload the key file to that exact path and redeploy.

http_error.title: The server did not return 200.
http_error.fix: Check for auth, WAF rules, or bot protection blocking unauthenticated requests.

redirected_off_host.title: The request was redirected to another host.
redirected_off_host.fix: The key file must resolve on the same host as the URLs you submit. Remove the cross-host redirect.

key_mismatch.title: The file content does not match the key.
key_mismatch.fix: The file body must contain the key and nothing else — watch for a byte-order mark or extra text.

empty_body.title: The file is empty.
empty_body.fix: Write the key into the file; an empty response fails verification.

html_response.title: The server returned HTML, not the key.
html_response.fix: This is usually a soft 404. Make sure the path is served as a static text file.

byte_order_mark.title: The file starts with a UTF-8 byte-order mark.
byte_order_mark.fix: The bytes then differ from the key even though the text looks identical. Re-save the file as UTF-8 without BOM.

body_too_large.title: The response is far larger than a key file should be.
body_too_large.fix: The file should contain only the key. Anything else means the wrong route is answering.

whenToUse.title: When to use submitnow IndexNow Key Checker
whenToUse.intro: An HTTP 403 or silent 202 drop from IndexNow almost always means search engines could not read your public key file cleanly. submitnow Key Checker reproduces that external fetch for free without requiring an account.

items.title: Before your first submission
items.description: Confirm the file is live before you spend a batch finding out that it is not.

items.title: After a deploy or migration
items.description: Static files are easy to lose when routing, hosting, or CDN rules change.

items.title: When Bing answers 403 or 422
items.description: Both codes usually trace back to the key file or a host mismatch rather than to the URL list itself.

items.title: When it loads for you but not for a crawler
items.description: Auth, WAF rules and geo-blocking make a file that opens fine in your browser invisible from the outside.

howTo.title: How to verify an IndexNow key file with submitnow
howTo.intro: The request is made server-side with redirects followed, so you see the same thing the search engine's fetcher would see.

steps.title: Enter the host
steps.description: Use the hostname your URLs live on, without a scheme or path — for example www.example.com.

steps.title: Enter the key
steps.description: The same key string you will pass in the submission. If the file sits at a non-default path, add it as the key file URL.

steps.title: Run the check
steps.description: The server fetches the file, follows redirects, and reports the final URL, status, content type and body.

steps.title: Fix anything reported
steps.description: Each issue lists the change that resolves it. Re-run until the result is clean, then submit your batch.

items.title: Cached CDN responses
items.description: A CDN can keep serving an old 404 after you upload the file. Purge that path, then re-check.

items.title: Trailing whitespace or a BOM
items.description: A UTF-8 byte-order mark makes the body differ from the key even when the two look identical on screen.

items.title: www or HTTPS redirects
items.description: A redirect that changes the hostname breaks verification even when it lands on a perfectly valid file.

items.title: Bot protection
items.description: Challenge pages return 200 with HTML. To a search engine that is a failed verification, not a security feature.

items.question: Why can this not run in my browser?
items.answer: A browser cannot read a cross-origin response without a CORS header, and key files are served as plain static text. The fetch has to happen server-side.

items.question: Does submitnow store the key I check?
items.answer: No. submitnow uses the key strictly in memory to fetch and compare the public response, then discards it with zero database or disk persistence.

items.question: The check passes but Bing still returns 403.
items.answer: Confirm the key in the submission matches exactly, and that the host you declare is the same host as every URL in the batch.

items.question: Can I check a key file on a staging domain?
items.answer: Yes, as long as the domain is publicly reachable. A file behind a VPN or basic auth cannot be verified by a search engine either.

items.question: What does a 202 response from IndexNow mean?
items.answer: The batch was accepted but the key has not been validated yet. Running this check tells you now whether that validation will pass.

whenToUse.intro: IndexNow rejects any batch whose URLs span multiple hosts, and duplicate URLs waste rate-limit budget. submitnow Batch Builder cleans, deduplicates, groups by exact hostname, and splits large lists into 10,000-URL chunks locally in your browser.

items.title: Exports from a CMS or crawler
items.description: Lists copied out of a spreadsheet or crawl report usually carry blank lines, tracking parameters and mixed hosts.

items.title: Multi-domain properties
items.description: One request covers one host. Split a combined list before you submit rather than after a 422.

items.title: Lists over 10,000 URLs
items.description: The protocol caps a request at 10,000 URLs. The summary tells you when a list needs splitting.

items.title: Hand-assembled lists
items.description: Manually gathered URLs are where typos and missing schemes hide.

howTo.title: How to build a clean IndexNow batch in submitnow
howTo.intro: Parsing, deduplication and grouping all happen as you type. Nothing is uploaded at any point.

steps.title: Paste or import the list
steps.description: One URL per line, or separated by spaces and commas. Plain-text and CSV files can be imported directly.

steps.title: Read the summary
steps.description: Valid, duplicate and invalid counts update live, along with how many distinct hosts the list covers.

steps.title: Fix the invalid entries
steps.description: Values that are not http(s) URLs are listed separately so you can correct them at the source.

steps.title: Send one group to the submitter
steps.description: Each group holds a single host. Copy a group, or send the first one straight into the submission form.

items.title: http and https treated as one URL
items.description: They share a hostname but are different URLs. Submit the canonical scheme only — in practice, https.

items.title: www and apex treated as interchangeable
items.description: www.example.com and example.com are separate hosts to IndexNow, and each needs its own key file.

items.title: Tracking parameters left in place
items.description: A URL with ?utm_source is a different URL. Submitting both wastes quota and can read as spam.

items.title: Redirecting or missing URLs in the batch
items.description: Notifying an engine about a URL that does not resolve is noise. Submit destinations, not redirects.

items.question: Why must all URLs share one host?
items.answer: The key file proves ownership of a single host, so an engine only accepts URLs on that host within the same request.

items.question: Does the tool request or validate the URLs?
items.answer: No. It checks syntax and grouping only, and never fetches the URLs. Nothing leaves your browser.

items.question: Are duplicates removed automatically?
items.answer: Yes. Exact duplicates are collapsed and the count is reported, so you can see how noisy the source list was.

items.question: What counts as invalid?
items.answer: Anything that is not an absolute http or https URL — relative paths, bare domains without a scheme, and empty lines.

items.question: Can I submit more than 10,000 URLs?
items.answer: The IndexNow protocol caps each HTTP request at 10,000 URLs. submitnow Batch Builder splits large host groups into 10,000-URL chunks automatically, and the main submitnow form also auto-submits lists over 10,000 URLs sequentially.

whenToUse.title: When to use submitnow Sitemap Diff for IndexNow
whenToUse.intro: Submitting your entire sitemap on every deploy is the fastest way to trigger IndexNow HTTP 429 rate limits. submitnow Sitemap Diff isolates only added, modified, or removed URLs — free, with no account required and zero server storage.

items.title: After a content deploy
items.description: Compare the sitemap before and after a release to get exactly the pages that release touched.

items.title: On a large site
items.description: When a sitemap holds thousands of entries, the changed set is usually a handful. Submit that instead.

items.title: When lastmod is reliable
items.description: If your generator writes accurate lastmod values, changed pages can be detected without crawling anything.

items.title: Auditing a release
items.description: The diff doubles as a record of which URLs a deploy added or modified.

howTo.title: How to diff sitemaps or filter by lastmod in submitnow
howTo.intro: Upload local .xml / .xml.gz files for 100% browser-side parsing, or fetch a public sitemap URL / nested sitemap index via submitnow’s stateless SSRF-guarded fetcher.

steps.title: Load your baseline (optional)
steps.description: Upload a previous .xml / .xml.gz file, fetch an earlier snapshot, or pick a baseline saved locally in your browser (up to 10,000 entries). Skip this step if you only need lastmod filtering on a single sitemap.

steps.title: Fetch live sitemap or upload current file
steps.description: Enter a bare domain (auto-discovers sitemaps from robots.txt) or sitemap URL — including .xml.gz and nested <sitemapindex> — or upload a local XML/gzip snapshot.

steps.title: Choose delta scope or lastmod window
steps.description: In diff mode, toggle Added, Changed (lastmod moved), and Removed URLs (to signal 404/410 deletions). In single-sitemap mode, filter by last 24h, 7d, or 30d.

steps.title: Send directly to submitnow or export
steps.description: Copy, download, or hand off the delta queue straight into the submitnow Batch Submitter, which auto-batches lists over 10,000 URLs.

items.title: Uploading a local sitemap index instead of fetching its URL
items.description: Local file uploads stay strictly offline and cannot fetch remote child sitemaps. To expand a <sitemapindex> automatically (up to 20 child files / 50,000 URLs), paste its public URL into the Fetch URL field instead.

items.title: Generators that restamp every lastmod
items.description: Some tools rewrite every lastmod on each build, which makes every URL look changed. Check before submitting the whole set.

items.title: Missing lastmod values
items.description: Without lastmod, only added URLs can be detected — an edit to an existing page is invisible to a diff.

items.title: Mixed hosts in one sitemap
items.description: A sitemap spanning several hosts produces a queue you still have to split before submitting.

items.question: When should I fetch a remote sitemap URL vs. upload local XML files in submitnow?
items.answer: Upload local .xml or .xml.gz files when you want 100% browser-only processing or need to diff staging files not on the public internet. Use submitnow’s Fetch URL field when you want automatic robots.txt discovery or nested <sitemapindex> expansion — remote fetches run statelessly in memory with SSRF protection and zero database storage.

items.question: How does submitnow detect a changed URL?
items.answer: In two-sitemap diff mode, any URL present in both snapshots whose <lastmod> value changed counts as Changed, URLs only in the newer snapshot count as Added, and URLs missing from the newer snapshot count as Removed.

items.question: Can submitnow export removed URLs for IndexNow?
items.answer: Yes. Removed URLs are counted and can be toggled into your export queue via the "Include removed URLs" checkbox so participating search engines re-crawl deleted pages and observe their HTTP 404/410 status promptly.

items.question: Does submitnow Sitemap Diff support gzipped (.xml.gz) sitemaps?
items.answer: Yes. Both local .xml.gz file uploads (decompressed directly in modern browsers) and remote .xml.gz sitemap URLs (up to 10 MB compressed / 25 MB decompressed) are supported automatically.

items.question: What if my sitemap diff queue exceeds 10,000 URLs?
items.answer: IndexNow accepts up to 10,000 same-host URLs per HTTP request. Send your queue straight to the submitnow Batch Submitter on the homepage and it will automatically split and submit sequential 10,000-URL batches.
